item.title: Flights normalizing after ground stop, FAA says. Here's what to know.
item.description: Officials attributed the ground stop to aging system infrastructure and legacy technology.

item.title: Taking a ride in a flying car
item.description: Flying cars have been parked in our imagination for more than a century, but a Bay Area startup, Alef, has spent 11 years trying to get the idea off the ground. Itay Hod takes a ride, getting a bird's-eye view of the future.

item.title: A look at the bridge linking China and North Korea
item.description: Asia has a new tourist attraction in an unlikely place: between China and North Korea. Anna Coren takes a look.

item.title: Pope Leo revisits Peruvian city where he once served as a missionary, bishop
item.description: Pope Leo wrapped up a historic visit to South America. He flew by helicopter to a mountainous area of Peru to celebrate Mass, where he once served as a missionary. Chris Livesay is traveling with the pontiff and has more.

item.title: Siblings of man run over by ICE agent say incident was "intentional"
item.description: Miguel Parra Hernandez was hit by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent Mario Alberto Morales in Houston on Oct. 10.

item.title: Siblings of man run over by ICE agent allege that "it was not an accident"
item.description: Last month, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in an unmarked SUV struck and injured a Mexican construction worker. Now, his siblings are speaking with Camilo Montoya-Galvez about the incident, alleging that "it was not an accident."

item.title: Trump officials ask for $50 billion for air traffic control after ground stop
item.description: President Trump broke his silence on the travel turmoil, triggered by Friday's nationwide ground stop. Taurean Small reports from the White House.

item.title: Ripple effects of nationwide ground stop still felt at airports: "Exhausted, frustrated"
item.description: The ripple effects of Friday's nationwide ground stop were still felt on Sunday, with 2,000 canceled flights and more than 8,000 delays. Gwen Baumgardner reports from Los Angeles International Airport.

item.title: Billy Evans tells his side of "You Can See Everything," Elizabeth Holmes' portrayal
item.description: In his first TV interview, Billy Evans, partner of disgraced Theranos co-founder Elizabeth Holmes, talks about his characterization in the documentary "You Can See Everything," as well as threats he says have been made against his family's safety.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Nov. 15)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Extended interview: Billy Evans on Elizabeth Holmes and "You Can See Everything"
item.description: In his first TV interview, Billy Evans talks with correspondent Matt Gutman about the portrayal of himself and his partner, disgraced Theranos co-founder Elizabeth Holmes, in the acclaimed Nathan Fielder-Lance Oppenheim documentary "You Can See Everything." He also discusses seeing "vulnerable" moments in the film being exposed to the world; his control of Holmes' social media; and his family's weekly visits to Holmes in prison. [Spoiler alert: This interview contains details of the film.]

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: John Malkovich on his career
item.description: John Malkovich says he couldn't teach the John Malkovich method—because there's no such thing—"and I certainly wouldn't recommend studying it."

item.title: Parents whose sons died from kratom use warn about the substance
item.description: Kratom is derived from a tree in Southeast Asia. Advocates say it can help with opioid addiction, while health experts say it can lead to death.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Kratom faces scrutiny over health concerns
item.description: Kratom products, sold at gas stations, have found allies in Washington. But health experts warn it is an addictive opioid, fueling increasing outrage that it remains legal in most states.

item.description: Next Sunday, 60 Minutes heads to a rodeo at the Louisiana State Penitentiary. The cowboys are prison inmates who've earned a chance to ride bulls and horses, something that gives them a sense of freedom.

item.description: The attacks come after the U.S. carried out minor strikes on Iran's Qeshm island in recent weeks.

item.title: Cassidy slams RFK Jr. for "series of failures" as HHS secretary
item.description: GOP Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana railed against Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for what he called a "series of failures" at the helm of the Department of Health and Human Services.

item.title: Vulcan rocket fails in major setback for United Launch Alliance
item.description: The loss of its new Vulcan rocket was the first outright failure for United Launch Alliance, a major setback in the commercial launch industry.

item.title: Ground stop shows "we have to get off old network," Duffy says
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that "we have to get off old network, old telecom" after a telecommunication outage led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

item.title: Army whistleblower alleges officials ignored warnings before Kuwait attack
item.description: Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom filed a complaint with Congress on Friday, saying Army leaders dismissed concerns about a U.S. command post in Kuwait. He will appear on 60 Minutes tonight.

item.title: U.S. reportedly floated trading Ukrainian land for NATO membership
item.description: The Ukrainian president said he would put the question of a potential exchange to the people if certain guarantees were in place.
